paragraphs: Rabbi Avdimi bar Nechunya, Midrash Tehillim 103:1.
Rav Kahana, son of Rav Nechunya, Taanit 24b.[^1][^2]

notes.text: These are separate patronymic attestations, not a proposed common-father identity.

Midrash Tehillim 103:1 reads Rabbi Avdimi beRabbi Nechunya. Berakhot 23b has Rav Yosef son of Rav Nechunya, and Taanit 24b has Rav Kahana son of Rav Nechunya. Hyman's shorter patronymic forms and alternative heading are retained. These are separate attestations; sharing Nechunya does not establish a common father.
